newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rolls-Royce, Cooper Cameron set up Russian JVs.
newsitem.headline: Rolls-Royce, Cooper Cameron set up Russian JVs.

text.p: British Rolls-Royce and U.S. Cooper Cameron Corporation on Tuesday signed an agreement with Russian engine company AO Lyulka-Saturn to set up joint ventures to develop gas turbine engines.

Viktor Chepkin, Lyulka-Saturn president and CEO, told a news conference that the Lyulka-Rolls-Royce venture would produce a new engine, called the AL31ST, for oil, gas and electrical power generation markets.
The engine's design will be based on Lyulka-Saturn's Sukhoi-27 fighter aircraft engine.
Chepkin said both agreements were signed after three years of negotiations with Western partners.
"We have invested 50 percent of the charter capital in each of these ventures," he said, declining to say how much had been invested in each venture.
Chepkin also said that the new engine would use Rolls-Royce technology to cut pollution.
Michael Grimes, Cooper Cameron president, said that the Lyulka-Cooper venture would incorporate Cooper Cameron's product packaging and compressor technology.
Chepkin said final details before starting the joint venture's work would be finished next month.
"We hope that Gazprom will be our main customer in Russia," he said, adding that the Russian gas giant has about 3,500 engines to pump gas. "Most of them must be replaced soon."
Chepkin said the ventures would produce the first engine later this year. "It may cost about $3 million," he added.
Robert Sunerton, Rolls-Royce managing director, said that the joint venture marked the first time the three countries had joined forces.
"There is a tremendous market in Russia for gas pumping," he said, adding that two-thirds of all gas pumping engines in the world are in the former Soviet Union.
Anatoly Boiko, Gazprom's senior manager in the gas transportation department, said his company would order gas pumping equipment from companies that had set up joint ventures with Russian firms.
"Gazprom needs about 100 engines annually," Boiko said.

Meanwhile, U.S. industrial giant General Electric Co, which has a joint venture with Russian company AO Rybinskiye Motory, said on Monday that it planned to produce its first gas pumping turbine, the LM-2500, by the end of this year.
A senior GE official said Gazprom could also be a potential customer for these turbines.
